I've been farming this land for 40 years. I know this soil, I know this weather, and I know what gives me a decent harvest. My wife and two sons help when they're not working in town, so I can't do anything too complicated. My well gives me enough water if I plan carefully. Here's how I see this year:

**Wheat and maize on the main plot (about 7 mu):** This rotation is what feeds my family and brings in steady cash. I'll use the improved wheat variety the village has been using for years — it does well here and the seed dealer knows it. Same with maize — I buy Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed like always. It's reliable. I apply fertilizer in two batches the way my father taught me, plus what the township agronomist said a few years back. Three irrigations for wheat, two for maize from my well.

**Cotton (the remaining 3.9 mu):** Cotton is harder work and prices have been up and down, but I keep some because it spreads my risk. I use the Bt hybrid cotton — far fewer bollworm sprays than the old days. But I still have to watch for aphids and whitefly. I plough this plot deeper because cotton roots need room.

I won't change much from last year. At my age, I do what I know works.
